2. Facts, in short, are that, the plaintiff instituted this Admiralty suit for recovery of US$ 19,92,000.00 on the allegation, inter alia, that the vessel M.V.Bengal Pride while being insured under Policy No. SBC/M (HULL) HO/POL/04/86 dated 6.4.86 suffered a grounding on or about 8.9.86 and sustained total damage. It was plaintiffs averment that no repair of the vessel could be made in Bangladesh or in India and it was impossible to tow the vessel in the monsoon to Singapore, Korea or Japan for repair. The plaintiff finally with leave of the Court sold the vessel, Bengal Pride, as a scrap for US $ 6,10,000 by obtaining a survey of the condition of the vessel before sale through Court. The defendant No. 1 by their telex dated 17.4.87 denied the claim of total loss or constructive loss as well as of unrepaired damage. It was plaintiffs case that the plaintiff as a prudent man had no other alternative but to cut the loss by selling vessel as a scrap. The claim of the plaintiff for total loss would be US$ 2,250,000 less the value of scrap for which it was sold viz US$ 6,10,000/- and the plaintiff is entitled to US$ 19,11,000/- and it the case of constructive it would be 5 years working loss if the vessel would run, @ the rate of net profit of 1000 dollars per day net. On being refused by the Insurance the plaintiff is constrained to file this Admiralty suit for a decree for US$ 19,10,000/- or, in the alternative, US$ 18,25,000/- and other relief as the Court may deem fit and proper. 

 10. Now coming to the point, in the instant case the vessel, namely M V. Bengal Pride, was mortgaged with the Sonali Bank, Motijheel Branch, Dhaka and Sonali Bank is one of the defendants in this case along with Sadharan Bima Corporation. The Sonali Bank has made an application to be transposed as a plaintiff on the ground that the Bank has also prior claim and need be paid and reference is made to the provisions of section 11 of the Admiralty Court Act, 1861. It appears, that similar provision existed in Bangladesh Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 1983 where it has been provided that a mortgagee shall be entitled to recover the amount due under the mortgage by appropriate proceeding in the High Court Division and when passing a decree or thereafter, the High Court Division may direct that the mortgaged ship or share be sold in execution of the decree. Therefore, it appears that the jurisdiction of High Court in such matters which concern marine insurance or maritime assurance arising out of such contracts and claims arising out of a marine mortgage is covered by section 11 of the Admiralty Courts Act of 1861 and by section 43 of the Bangladesh Merchant Shipping Ordinance. In that view of the matter I find that this Court is competent to hear this application and to proceed on merit. This application for return of the plaint, therefore, is rejected.
